minutes.headline: Town Meeting approved the Bright Farms lettuce greenhouse tax break, street light purchase, and stormwater bylaw changes.
minutes.summary: The November 2020 Special Town Meeting adjusted the FY21 budget, funded deferred capital projects, bought the street lights, and made deposits to stabilization and OPEB. It approved two union contracts, a gift of conservation land, a TIF agreement with Mass Greenhouse (Bright Farms), land transfers to Conservation, and the stormwater bylaw update. A quorum challenge near the end was settled by a hand count and the last article passed.

what_happened.line: Town Meeting approved the tax agreement (TIF) with Mass Greenhouse LLC (Bright Farms) by a clear majority after long debate.
Voters approved buying the street lights, with more than two-thirds in favor but not unanimous.
The stormwater bylaw amendment passed by majority, with a few opposed over costs and property rights.
Funds were approved for FY21 budget transfers, deferred capital projects, and deposits to stabilization and OPEB; the two union contracts passed with some opposed.
A quorum challenge near the end was settled by hand count, and the meeting finished the last article.

why_it_matters: The greenhouse agreement exempts a company from part of its property taxes for eight years in exchange for expected new revenue and jobs, so it affects what that property pays toward the tax base.
The street light purchase, the contract raises and the savings and OPEB deposits shape future town costs and tax bills, and the stormwater bylaw may add study costs for some private landowners.
